Beyond the visible lesion: mycotoxin attenuation and spatial heterogeneity in maize cobs
nodes.venue: Mycotoxin Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visible mould is widely used as a practical sorting cue in maize, but it remains unclear whether the visible lesion marks the boundary of mycotoxin contamination within an intact cob. This study examined mycotoxin attenuation, spatial heterogeneity, and co-occurrence in visibly mouldy white maize cobs, using measured distances from the visible mould margin. Cobs with visible mould ( n = 35) were sampled for the study. For each cob, the visible mould margin was coded as 0 mm, and adjacent sections were collected at the 50% and 75% points along the measured distance from the lesion boundary to the distal cob tip, resulting in 98 cob-section observations. Mycotoxins, FUMs (FB1, FB2, FB3), deoxynivalenol (DON), zearalenone (ZEA), nivalenol (NIV) and AF (AFB1) were quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Samples with no detectable levels of mycotoxins were replaced with zero, and total FUMs were calculated (FB1 + FB2 + FB3). The visible mould margin accounted for the largest share of the measured toxin burden, accounting for 84.4% of total FUM, 89.4% of DON, 77.8% of ZEA, and 92.2% of NIV. Adjacent sections retained measurable residual mycotoxins, including 15.6% of total FUM, 10.6% of DON, 22.2% of ZEA, and 7.8% of NIV. In full-distance models, DON, ZEA, and NIV declined significantly with distance, whereas total FUM did not show significant monotonic attenuation. The AFB1 was detected in only three cob sections; these detections co-occurred with Fusarium -associated toxins. Co-occurrence analysis showed that adjacent sections frequently remained positive for multiple Fusarium -associated toxin groups, with the FUM + DON + ZEA profile persisting across measured-distance bands. These findings show that visible mould is a useful warning signal but not a reliable toxicological boundary. The results support cob-level rejection or segregation of visibly mouldy cobs before shelling, rather than lesion-level trimming, as a more defensible food-safety control measure.

nodes.name: Breaking GUI Agent Actions: Realistic Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal LLMs
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has enabled GUI agents that interpret interface screenshots and execute natural-language instructions. However, their increasing role in human–computer interaction raises security concerns. Existing work shows that MLLMs are highly sensitive to interface perturbations, yet most attacks assume unrealistic capabilities such as direct access to model-ready inputs. In real deployments, attackers cannot control the screenshot pipeline or the non-differentiable preprocessing operations preceding inference, rendering many prior attacks ineffective. We introduce Realistic Adversarial Attack (RAA) framework that models the complete screenshot-to-prediction pipeline. To address gradient blockage from non-differentiable preprocessing (e.g., resizing and quantization), we develop a dual-branch differentiable preprocessing module that restores gradient flow while remaining faithful to the actual inference path. To improve robustness against query phrasing changes, we further incorporate a task-level semantic variation mechanism that jointly optimizes over paraphrased task variants. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct and GUI-Owl-7B show that RAA consistently outperforms prior attacks, improving attack success rates by an average of 30% under localized perturbations and a 10.7% under global perturbations, while maintaining strong effectiveness against standard defenses such as resizing, compression, and noise. Ablation studies highlight the roles of perturbation region and semantic diversity. Our framework establishes a practical threat model for GUI agents and offers a foundation for future robustness and security research.

nodes.name: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
A Physics‐Informed Two‐Stage Retrieval Method for EMIT Remote Sensing Methane Plumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite missions, particularly EMIT, have revolutionized methane point source monitoring. However, current operational retrieval pipelines typically rely on physically‐based matched filters followed by labor‐intensive manual verification to mitigate high false alarm rates caused by complex background interference. This dependence on human intervention restricts the scalability and efficiency required for rapid, automated global monitoring. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Plume‐Net, a novel Physics‐Informed Guided Two‐Stage Retrieval Method. Unlike conventional approaches, Plume‐Net decouples the task into a “global existence classification” stage and a “local pixel‐level regression” stage to maximize reliability without human‐in‐the‐loop. The core innovation lies in the integration of physical priors with deep learning: In the first stage, a Physics‐Informed Spectral Gating (PISG) module explicitly injects methane spectral absorption knowledge into the network, dynamically recalibrating channel weights to suppress background noise. In the second stage, to overcome the difficulties of regressing sparse, long‐tail plume distributions, we propose a Plume‐Focused Sampling Strategy and an Intensity‐Aware Pixel‐Level Weighted Loss function, forcing the network to prioritize rare but critical high‐concentration signals. Evaluated on real‐world EMIT observations, Plume‐Net achieves an ROC‐AUC of 0.961 in detection and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 33.33 ppm·m in quantification. By significantly reducing false positives while maintaining high precision, this method offers a robust, fully automated alternative to current semi‐manual retrieval workflows.

nodes.name: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
nodes.abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

nodes.name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
A localization and quantification method of Fe <sub>3</sub> O <sub>4</sub> magnetic nanoparticles based on MRX and unscented Kalman filter
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) have attracted extensive research attention in the field of nanomedicine owing to their distinctive magnetic properties and relaxation behaviors. Nevertheless, accurate localization and quantitative estimation of MNPs remain challenging under harsh measurement conditions, such as ultra-low particle concentration and low signal-to-noise ratio. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, we develop an MNP point-source localization and quantification approach integrating magnetic relaxometry and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF). By combining the relaxation theoretical model—moment superposition model and point-source forward model into a unified measurement model, this method fully leverages the time-varying evolution information contained in relaxation signals. Moreover, the UKF is further employed to realize the joint state estimation of particle spatial coordinates and mass. Multiple replicate measurements are performed on physical gel phantoms via a custom-built platform for magnetization and relaxation signal acquisition. Experimental results reveal that the proposed method achieves localization precision superior to 1 mm, with mass quantification errors below 30 μ g. Compared with conventional linear reconstruction approaches, this UKF-based method exhibits stronger robustness against residual sinusoidal noise and system nonlinear dynamics, and its superiority is particularly prominent in the detection of trace amounts of particles. A comprehensive technical framework covering signal acquisition, data preprocessing and nonlinear state estimation is established in this work, yielding a systematic scheme for accurate localization and quantification of MNPs. Significant application prospects can be anticipated for the presented approach in magnetic particle imaging, targeted drug delivery monitoring, in vivo tracer detection and other relevant disciplines.

nodes.name: Implementation of self-declare policy in halal certification in Indonesia: challenges, policy model, and integration of maqāṣid al-sharīʿa
nodes.venue: Journal of Islamic Marketing
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the implementation of Indonesia’s self-declared halal certification policy for micro and small enterprises (MSE), identifies its challenges and proposes a policy framework that integrates maqāṣid al-sharīʿa principles to improve its effectiveness, equity and compliance. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study was conducted among halal certification institutions (LP3H) in Java: State Islamic University (UIN) Walisongo Semarang, State Islamic University (UIN) Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta, Institute of Islamic Studies (IAI) Ngawi and State Islamic University (UIN) Raden Mas Said Surakarta. This study included LP3H managers, three halal product process assistants (PPH) who mentored more than 500 MSEs and seven MSE owners from Ponorogo in food production. MSE participants were identified through field outreach and the 3rd National Coordination Meeting of LP3H in Jakarta on June 7, 2024, which revealed 20 cases of administrative and substantive errors in self-declare. Data collection involved interviews, focus group discussions and field observations, including the socialization of Sertifikasi Halal Gratis (SEHATI; Free Halal Certification) services conducted by the Ponorogo Halal Center. Findings The implementation faces structural and operational bottlenecks, including inadequate coordination among LP3H, PPH and MSE actors, a disconnect between strategic aims (consumer protection and economic empowerment) and practices and weak supervisory mechanisms. These gaps constrain inclusive participation and halal compliance. This study advances a public policy framework grounded in maqāṣid al-sharīʿa that emphasizes collaborative governance, regulatory clarity and balanced ethical and economic objectives. Research limitations/implications This study had certain limitations that should be considered. The analysis focused on LP3H and PPH in Java, which may not fully represent the conditions in other regions of Indonesia. In addition, it examined only the self-declared halal certification scheme and did not compare it with the regular certification process. Future research could address these limitations by including a broader geographic scope, involving a larger and more diverse range of institutions and incorporating a comparative analysis of different certification models to provide a more comprehensive understanding of policy implementation and its impacts. Practical implications First, regulatory bodies must standardize the Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification (KBLI) and establish minimum documentation standards across all LP3H institutions to prevent inconsistent halal governance outcomes. Second, at the institutional level, sustained multisector collaboration between the Government of Indonesia, universities and religious organizations is essential for building field-level capacity that goes beyond compliance targets. Third, from a normative standpoint, the maqāṣid al-sharīʿa framework must serve not only as an evaluative lens but also as a design principle for future policy reforms, ensuring that consumer protection and social justice remain central to halal governance. Theoretically, this study contributes by repositioning the maqāṣid al-sharīʿa framework from a purely evaluative lens into a design principle for halal policy and advances the literature on assisted self-declaration by specifying the institutional conditions under which decentralized certification can remain credible. For future research, these implications open avenues for testing the framework across sectors and comparative work on how the ethical-economic balance is sustained in different regulatory settings. Originality/value Existing research has focused on regulation, technology and institutional reform in halal certification; however, little attention has been paid to how Indonesia’s self-declared model works in practice in Indonesia. This study addresses this gap by foregrounding MSE experiences and institutional responses from LP3H and PPH and proposing a maqāṣid-based framework to strengthen the field-level implementation and consumer trust.

nodes.name: Data representation matters: Optimising machine learning for X-ray source classification by leveraging spatio-spectral information
nodes.venue: Astronomy & Astrophysics
nodes.abstract: Distinguishing between faint extended X-ray sources, such as galaxy clusters, and point-like sources, primarily active galactic nuclei (AGNs), is a fundamental yet challenging task in X-ray surveys, which are crucial to cosmological studies and astrophysical source population analyses. This paper presents a benchmark comparison of convolutional neural network models for classifying simulated observations of AGNs and galaxy clusters, focussing on the impact of data representation and interpretability of those data. XMM-Newton We systematically evaluated 1D, 2D, 2D+1D, and 3D CNNs trained on distinct data representations derived from simulated observations of AGNs and clusters: 1D (spectral), 2D (imaging), and 3D (event cube) data. Our experimental design leverages the physical constraints of the apparent size–redshift relation to ensure realistic source populations at fixed flux limits. We further applied 3D-GradCAM to interpret the learned features and assess the physical basis for the model's decision making to move beyond black-box classification. XMM-Newton Our results demonstrate that increased spectral resolution enhances classifier performance using 1D data and 2D spatial information provides a strong morphological baseline, the integration of both domains yields significant diagnostic gains. We find that a 3D CNN architecture applied directly to spatio-spectral event cubes provides the most robust performance, with superior consistency across cross-validation folds. Interpretability analysis reveals that the 3D model autonomously learns to distinguish the diffuse thermal emission of the intracluster medium from the localised, non-thermal power-law signatures of AGNs. The 3D CNN exploits multi-dimensional correlations that are lost in lower dimensional projections. While the performance gain over combined 2D and 1D baselines is marginal, the 3D approach demonstrates an inherent ability to perform an implicit background characterisation. By operating directly on total photon counts within event cubes, this method bypasses the need for manual background subtraction and modelling, offering a consistent, streamlined, end-to-end pipeline for the automated classification of X-ray sources in large-scale catalogues.

nodes.name: Assessment of Land Use Change and Mangrove Ecosystem Extent Using Google Earth Engine Based on the Random Forest Model
nodes.venue: ENVIBILITY: Journal of Environmental and Sustainability Studies
nodes.abstract: Batam City, designated a National Strategic Area and Free Trade Zone, has undergone rapid urbanization, industrialization, and infrastructure development that drive land use change. This study analyzes land use dynamics in Batam City from 1995 to 2025 using Landsat imagery processed in Google Earth Engine (GEE). A Random Forest classifier produced six classes: water bodies, built-up areas, vegetation, mangroves, agricultural land, and open land. Accuracy was assessed using Overall Accuracy (OA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), User’s Accuracy (UA), and the Kappa coefficient. The classification was highly accurate, with an OA of 97.38% and Kappa of 96.57% in 1995, and an OA of 99.49% and Kappa of 99.29% in 2025. Over 30 years, built-up areas expanded by 188.22 km², whereas agricultural land declined by 198.95 km² and mangroves by 22.06 km² (9.84%); vegetation and water bodies increased. Land use transformation was thus dominated by built-up expansion, reducing productive land and increasing pressure on coastal ecosystems. These findings can inform more adaptive spatial planning policies and support sustainable land use management.

nodes.name: ENVIBILITY: Journal of Environmental and Sustainability Studies
Speaker-Wise Dementia Screening fromNaturalistic Speech with Lexical Entropy, Semantic Drift, and Multimodal Fusion
nodes.abstract: Abstract Although advances have been made in dementia symptom management, early detection during stages when interventions are most effective remains a significant challenge. Most speech-based screening methods are evaluated using controlled elicitation tasks, often without examining how feature strength changes in the years preceding formal diagnosis. This study introduces a multimodal approach for dementia risk screening from naturalistic speech, integrating four traditional lexical features, two computational markers (lexical entropy from a probabilistic language model and semantic drift from sentence-level embeddings), and eGeMAPSv02 acoustic biomarkers. The framework is assessed on the DementiaNet corpus using speaker-disjoint nested group cross-validation. The optimal configuration, late fusion with stacked blending, achieves an AUC of 0.607 at the speaker level. Time-to-diagnosis stratified analysis demonstrates statistically significant discrimination in near-diagnostic windows, with text features peaking in the 5-year bin (AUC = 0.678) and acoustic features at the year of diagnosis (AUC = 0.640, p = 0.024). Exploratory analysis of more distant temporal bins (10 and 15 years) indicates that computational features may retain discriminative value where traditional features do not, although these patterns do not reach statistical significance with the current sample size. These findings support further investigation of computational language features alongside traditional and acoustic markers in larger longitudinal studies of speech-based dementia screening.

nodes.name: SimuScan-Agent: language-model orchestration of synthetic-data-driven autonomous atomic force microscopy
nodes.abstract: Abstract Atomic force microscopy (AFM) enables nanoscale characterization, but large-area investigations remain slow and require coordination of data preparation, model training and instrument operation. Here we introduce SimuScan-Agent, an LLM-orchestrated framework that translates natural-language objectives into adaptive AFM workflows. Combining multimodal morphological sources with physics-informed simulation, it generates annotated synthetic datasets without manual per-image labeling, trains and deploys segmentation and representation-learning models, and guides acquisition using online detections and class-specific sampling objectives. In simulations, probabilistic active exploration reduced measurements and sampled area by approximately 71% relative to raster scanning. Experimentally, SimuScan-Agent explored a ~10 mm² region by sampling 17.2% of available positions, estimating class-specific spatial distributions and assembling a morphological library to identify representative and atypical nanostructures. By linking synthetic-data generation, machine learning and adaptive acquisition through natural-language interaction, the framework lowers barriers to goal-directed nanoscale studies and offers a foundation for more intelligent, autonomous AFM systems that adapt experimental decisions to what they learn during measurement.

nodes.name: Semantic-Aware Visual Scene Understanding for Classroom Behavior Perception via Equipment Relations
nodes.venue: International Journal on Semantic Web and Information Systems
nodes.abstract: Intelligent monitoring of industry-education practical training requires reliable recognition of teaching events involving people, equipment, and workstations. However, visually similar devices, occlusion, idle equipment, and incidental proximity often create ambiguous evidence. This study proposed an equipment-relation guided framework for teaching behavior detection. The model detected persons, equipment, and workstations and formed relation units encoding spatial affiliation and instructional relevance. An equipment participation gate integrated operation responses, relation priors, workstation consistency, and background-confusion cues, while a short-term temporal module improved robustness to occlusion and transient motion. The equipment-relation guided framework recognized teacher demonstration, student operation, teacher guidance, student observation, and risky operation. On the two datasets developed in this study, it improved F1-score by 5.99 and 5.96 percentage points and mean average precision@0.5:0.95 by 6.73 and 6.78 percentage points over the baseline. Ablation, significance, complexity, and visualization analyses confirmed its effectiveness.

nodes.name: International Journal on Semantic Web and Information Systems
Oxygen Vacancy–Modified WO3 for Advanced Photoelectrochemical H2S Sensing via Synergistic Interfacial and Surface Optimization
nodes.venue: ACS Sensors
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), a corrosive and extremely poisonous gas, poses serious threats to environmental security and human health, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and stable room-temperature sensing technologies. Conventional gas sensors are often limited by high operating temperatures and rapid deactivation. Herein, a solar-driven photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor for room-temperature gas sensing is developed by precisely controlling the oxygen vacancies (VOs) concentration in WO3, which optimizes interfacial transport and surface reaction kinetics. The results of integrated differential phase contrast imaging, in situ PEC characterization, and computational simulations collectively reveal that VOs improve the spatial separation of photoexcited carriers, optimize interfacial contact and charge transfer kinetics, and lower the adsorption energy of O2 and H2S, which accelerates surface reactions. The optimized sensor delivers a 67-fold enhancement in the room-temperature H2S response compared with pristine WO3, along with excellent stability, high selectivity, and a part per billion-level detection limit. This work provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance, room temperature-operable, light-excited, thick-film electrode sensors via interface–surface synergistic enhancement.

nodes.name: Oblique Back-Illumination Microscopy Enables Phase-Gradient Optical Sensing of Malaria-Induced Intracellular Heterogeneity
nodes.venue: ACS Omega
nodes.abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a major global health burden, with diagnosis often relying on ex vivo analysis of infected red blood cells (RBCs), which incompletely samples key stages of parasite development. In particular, early ring-stage parasites exhibit subtle structural perturbations, while a significant fraction of parasite burden─including immature gametocytes─is sequestered within the microvasculature and is not readily captured in peripheral blood smears. Here, we present a label-free imaging and analysis framework that integrates oblique back-illumination microscopy (OBM) with data-driven classification to detect malaria infection by sensing parasite-induced intracellular heterogeneity. Unlike stained brightfield microscopy and quantitative phase imaging (QPI) methods that depend on interferometric acquisition and phase reconstruction, OBM directly converts intracellular refractive-index gradients into measurable intensity variations through noninterferometric phase-gradient contrast. By exploiting multiply scattered illumination and asymmetric detection, OBM enhances sensitivity to parasite-induced refractive-index gradients associated with Plasmodium falciparum development, capturing morphological complexity across the intraerythrocytic lifecycle. This enables the discrimination of uninfected cells, early ring-stage infections, and mature gametocytes. Fourier-domain analysis further reveals infection-stage-dependent redistribution of spatial-frequency content, providing a physically interpretable description of progressive intracellular remodeling during parasite development. Using synchronized in vitro cultures with brightfield validation, we demonstrate automated classification of infected RBCs with accuracies of 95% for binary classification and 82% for multiclass classification, with consistent precision, recall, and F1-scores across repeated randomized data splits. Together, these results establish OBM as a scalable, label-free sensing strategy that leverages intracellular heterogeneity as a diagnostic signal while providing access to stage-resolved optical phenotypes that remain difficult to interrogate with existing approaches. By building on prior studies of in vivo phase-gradient imaging, this framework provides a pathway toward integrating OBM with real-time analysis for noninvasive and field-deployable malaria diagnostics, particularly where conventional ex vivo measurements are limited by parasite sequestration.

nodes.name: Nowcasting Meso-Level Industrial Production Using Multi-Source Satellite Data and Hybrid DFM–Machine Learning Framework
nodes.abstract: Abstract Official industrial statistics are released with delays, creating a need for timely complementary information. This study evaluates whether freely available multi-source satellite observations can nowcast Japan’s Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and production indicators for chemicals, ordinary steel, and four-wheel motor vehicles. Daily VIIRS nighttime-light and Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI NO₂ observations from major production sites over July 2018–December 2025 were summarized using dynamic factor models (DFMs). Ridge regression and LightGBM were evaluated against direct-regression and autoregressive benchmarks using cross-validation. The optimal specification differed across targets. The IIP was best predicted by LightGBM using nighttime lights, NO₂, lagged IIP, and five factors without blocks. Chemicals favored NO₂, lagged target values, regional factors, and ridge regression; steel favored combined satellite data, firm-level factors, and ridge regression without lagged targets. For automobiles, ridge regression using nighttime lights from selected Toyota and Mazda plants outperformed both the all-firm satellite model and AR(1) benchmark. DFM-based models reduced RMSE relative to direct regression for all targets. These findings show that free satellite data provide useful predictive information, but effective nowcasting requires target-specific choices of satellite signals, factor structure, prediction model, and observation sites.

nodes.name: Multimodal Fusion of Visual and Gyroscopic Data for Road Surface Monitoring Using ResNet50-Based Transfer Learning
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Driven by climate change and escalating traffic, rapid road deterioration threatens public safety, prompting a shift from costly manual inspections toward scalable solutions. High-precision laser scanners offer accuracy, but prohibitive costs limit continuous monitoring across extensive road networks. To overcome these constraints, this study proposes an automated multimodal monitoring system integrating real-time video imagery with gyroscopic impact data. The architecture employs a late fusion approach, combining visual features extracted from the Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer of a pre-trained ResNet50 model with synchronized gyroscopic time-series data. Experimental results revealed that while the initial baseline model achieved a recall of 0.75 and an F1-score of 0.55, applying data balancing enhanced performance, increasing the recall to 0.98 and the F1-score to 0.65. When evaluated on a geographically independent highway section, the model identified 44 bad road segments and encompassed 94% of actual bad segment durations, predicting a total duration of 741 s compared to the ground-truth 564 s. Ultimately, despite a tendency for over-detection, the model demonstrates significant practical utility as a conservative decision-support tool for proactive road maintenance due to its high sensitivity and robust detection capabilities.

nodes.name: Monitoring seasonal and long-term forest canopy dynamics using Sentinel-2 imagery and Random Forest on the Google Earth Engine platform
nodes.venue: PLOS One
nodes.abstract: Understanding forest canopy dynamics is critical for assessing the condition, resilience, and conservation priorities of protected landscapes. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal and seasonal variation in mapped forest canopy density within the Orchha Wildlife Sanctuary, Madhya Pradesh, India, using multi-seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery and a Google Earth Engine (GEE)-based Random Forest (RF) classification framework. Sentinel-2 data for pre-monsoon (March–May) and post-monsoon (October–December) periods in 2016 and 2024 were analyzed independently. Canopy-density information was derived from NDVI, NDMI, elevation, slope, and GLCM texture features and classified into four classes: non-forest, open, moderate, and dense canopy. The same RF procedure was applied to all four season-year datasets using NDVI-informed canopy-density strata and balanced reference sampling. Overall accuracy ranged from 97.80% to 98.95%, with Kappa coefficients of 0.970–0.986. The results indicated clear seasonal and interannual redistribution of mapped canopy-density classes. During the pre-monsoon period, non-forest and open classes decreased by 39.62% and 7.15%, respectively, while moderate and dense classes increased by 231.64% and 240.43%. During the post-monsoon period, moderate canopy increased by 26.01%, whereas dense canopy decreased by 9.46%. Within the common comparison area of 4,533.54 ha, transition analysis revealed substantial class persistence and redistribution, particularly among adjacent canopy-density classes such as open-to-moderate and dense-to-moderate transitions. Spatial changes were distributed across riparian, interior, and peripheral zones. Because 2016 used Level-1C top-of-atmosphere data and 2024 used Level-2A surface-reflectance products, interannual differences should be interpreted as changes in mapped canopy-density classes rather than precise biophysical changes in canopy structure. The framework provides a replicable approach for seasonal forest monitoring and spatially targeted conservation planning.

nodes.name: Mode-Aware Production Forecasting of Coalbed Methane Wells via Unsupervised Parameter-Image Clustering and Similarity-Based GAF Correction
nodes.venue: Energy & Fuels
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate and efficient production forecasting is critical for coalbed methane (CBM) well development and management. However, conventional engineering methods rely heavily on physical assumptions and parameter calibration, whereas direct data-driven models typically establish a global input–output mapping without explicitly distinguishing different production patterns or exploiting similarities among samples, thereby limiting their forecasting accuracy and generalizability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a structured forecasting framework integrating parameter-image representation, unsupervised clustering, lightweight classification, and similarity-based correction. Geological and development parameters are first converted into grayscale images, and spectral clustering combined with K-means++ is used to identify production-related modes. A MobileNetV2-based classifier is then trained to determine the mode category of new samples. Within the identified category, the most similar sample is retrieved, and its production sequences are encoded as Gramian Angular Field (GAF) images. Difference-image-guided posterior correction is further applied before reconstructing the corrected images into production time series. Results based on numerical simulation samples show that the proposed framework achieves high accuracy for both gas and water production forecasting, with R2 values of 0.99 and 0.99 for daily gas and daily water production, respectively. Compared with representative machine-learning and deep-learning models, the proposed method demonstrates superior accuracy and efficiency, indicating its potential for rapid CBM production forecasting.

nodes.name: Machine Vision and Network RTK-Based Miss-Seeding Detection and Compensation System for Potato Planting: Design and Integration
nodes.venue: Agriculture
nodes.abstract: To address the limitations of existing potato miss-seeding detection, including vulnerability to dust and vibration, lack of whole-process information management, and delayed reseeding response, this paper develops and verifies a miss-seeding detection and reseeding system for electric-driven potato planters based on machine vision and network Real-Time Kinematic (RTK). The system integrates an industrial camera, a network RTK rover station, and an STM32 microcontroller. A lightweight vision model enables efficient seed spoon identification. Miss-seeding events are real-time bound to high-precision RTK coordinates, with spatial distribution visualized through empirical GCJ-02 offset conversion and a map engine. PWM technology is applied to dynamically adjust the seed-metering belt motor speed for rapid compensation. Bench and field tests indicate that the miss-seeding detection rate exceeded 90% only in the workshop-calibrated, well-lit, no-seed specificity test; under normal field seeding conditions, it was approximately 83–85%, decreasing to about 64% under plant shading with an uncalibrated camera. The reseeding success rate reached approximately 87% at 0.3 m/s. This system achieves full-link closed-loop control and provides a technical solution for intelligent potato seeding.This study should be regarded as a proof-of-concept rather than a field-ready commercial solution.

nodes.name: Learning-based modality selection for efficient multimodal retrieval
nodes.venue: Discover Computing
nodes.abstract: Abstract Existing multimodal retrieval-augmented systems (RAG) typically retrieve both text and images for every query, including queries that can be answered using only textual information. This wastes computational resources and increases latency. We frame modality selection as a supervised classification problem in which a lightweight classifier determines whether visual retrieval is necessary, and we evaluate two variants based on when this decision is made. In the post-retrieval case, the classifier relies on image-relevance features and therefore requires image retrieval for every query; it can only save the time spent processing the retrieved images. The pre-retrieval-only classifier uses four features available after text retrieval and before visual retrieval, allowing the visual branch to be skipped for text-only queries. On a collection of 265 labeled queries over a corpus of 5,000 images, the pre-retrieval-only variant achieves 94.34% accuracy (95% Wilson interval [84.6%, 98.1%]; n = 53), with 1 unnecessary visual retrieval and 2 missed visual retrievals, while reducing measured pipeline latency from 118.97 to 65.61 ms per query, a 44.85% reduction. We compare the proposed variants with ten baselines. A query-only classifier using no retrieval information achieves 98.11%, indicating that a substantial portion of the label signal in this dataset can be recovered from the query surface form. The contribution therefore lies in the pre-retrieval routing architecture and its measured efficiency rather than classifier performance. Labels were produced by two annotators external to the author group, with Cohen’s kappa of 0.947 and complete agreement on the held-out test split. The main limitations are the small evaluation set, the fact that the queries were written by the authors, and the caption-only text corpus.

nodes.name: GraphLane: a spatio-temporal graph learning framework for lane localization
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Introduction Lane localization is an important component of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous driving, where accurate estimation of lane geometry is essential for safe vehicle navigation. Nevertheless, the current lane detection algorithms may face difficulties in complex driving situations due to poor visual feature extraction, unstable temporal prediction, and inadequate modeling of structural relations between lanes. Methods In order to overcome these issues, this paper introduces the unified spatio-temporal graph learning approach that integrates spatial feature extraction, temporal context aggregation, uncertainty-driven graph formation, graph attention reasoning, and geometric optimization. The proposed GraphLane framework dynamically learns graph connections between lane keypoints while incorporating uncertainty estimation to suppress unreliable feature interactions and temporal consistency to improve structural stability across consecutive frames. A geometry-aware optimization strategy is further introduced to encourage smooth and physically consistent lane predictions. The framework was evaluated on the CULane test set using the proposed row-anchor-based lane-existence and localization evaluation. Results Experimental results show that the proposed GraphLane framework achieves a lane-existence precision of 0.9769, recall of 0.8990, F1-score of 0.9363, and an average localization error of 19.28 pixels. Qualitative analysis shows that the framework produces smooth and consistent lane predictions under occlusions, shadows, dense traffic, and nighttime conditions. Discussion Other analyses on learned graphs, computational complexity, and ablation studies also show that incorporating temporal context, adaptive graph reasoning, and geometrically informed optimizations is effective for lane localization.

nodes.name: Fuzzy trust-based secure localization with CNN intrusion detection and RANSAC-GDA for wireless sensor networks
nodes.venue: Discover Computing
nodes.abstract: Abstract Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have made possible many applications like environment tracking, healthcare, smart cities, etc. However, reliable node localization remains challenging due to energy constraints, noisy range estimates, and malicious adversaries. This paper proposes a hybrid secure and energy-efficient localization framework that integrates Distributed Energy-Efficient Clustering (DEEC), Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC), and a Gaussian Distribution Approach (GDA) to enable robust position estimation. In addition, a lightweight Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a SMOTE-assisted Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is deployed at the pre-localization stage to identify and exclude malicious nodes, including Sybil behavior and falsified localization information. DEEC-RANSAC-GDA facilitates energy-efficient selection for cluster head formation, mitigates localization outliers via RANSAC, and optimizes localization using Gaussian probabilistic models. Implementation of the proposed IDS on the CIC-IDS-2017 benchmark dataset achieved 99.83% accuracy, 99.00% precision, 99.84% recall, and 99.42% F1-score, along with minimizing localization errors falling within the range of 0.46 m-0.53 m compared to DV-Hop and Weighted Hyperbolic Localization schemes.

nodes.name: From stretch﻿able materials and functional fibers to intelligent textile sensing systems
nodes.venue: Communications Materials
nodes.abstract: Abstract Wearable sensors that offer significant adaptability and comfort demonstrate substantial potential for discrete, seamless integration into garments, enabling diverse applications for remote monitoring. The transformation of rigid electronic devices into flexible and stretchable sensors, achieved by integrating conductive materials with compliant dielectrics, has enabled the development of robust sensors. However, several factors must be addressed to enable widespread adoption, including garment integration, wireless communication, data pipelines, signal processing, multimodal fusion, privacy and security concerns. Addressing these challenges is essential for establishing the technological and social infrastructure necessary for the widespread adoption of wearable technologies. This review highlights innovations in material and mechanical design strategies that have shaped the current landscape of wearables, and points out some remaining challenges.

nodes.name: Elevation-moderated thermal controls on Snow Melt Sensitivity: a remote sensing-based SMSI framework for Gulmarg in Jammu and Kashmir, India
nodes.venue: Bulletin of Geography. Physical Geography Series
nodes.abstract: Snowmelt conditions in high-altitude environments are increasingly influenced by rising temperatures, changing climatic conditions and local topography. The present study develops a multispectral geospatial framework to draw a Snow Melt Sensitivity Index (SMSI) for the Gulmarg region of Jammu and Kashmir using Landsat-9 OLI/TIRS and SRTM-DEM datasets. Four multispectral snow indices, namely Normalised Difference Snow Index (NDSI), Normalised Difference Snow-Cover Index (NDSCI), Normalised Difference Snow Moisture Index (NDSMI) and Snow Wetness Index (SWI) were integrated with Land Surface Temperature (LST) and elevation data. All variables were standardised using Z-score normalisation and weighted objectively through Principal Component Analysis (PCA). SMSI classification indicates that 67.79% of the region falls under moderate melt sensitivity, while 16.54% lies in high to very high sensitivity zones, primarily below 3,000 m elevation. Strong positive correlation between LST and SMSI (r=0.72) confirms thermal dominance in melt processes. The findings highlight elevation-moderated thermal control over snow dynamics and provide a robust framework for climate-sensitive mountain hydrology assessment.

Comparative use of remote sensing and in-situ data for chlorophyll-a estimation in urban lakes: a case study of Chitgar Lake, Tehran, Iran
nodes.venue: Bulletin of Geography. Physical Geography Series
nodes.abstract: Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is a key indicator of phytoplankton biomass and freshwater quality and is strongly influenced by nutrient availability, seasonal variability and climatic conditions. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of Chl-a in Chitgar Lake, an artificial urban lake in Tehran, Iran, by integrating long-term in-situ observations (2013–2025) with satellite-derived estimates from Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8. Seasonal analysis revealed that Chl-a concentrations were highest during summer (mean: 2.93 mg/m³), peaking in August (3.53 mg/m³), coinciding with elevated water temperatures (up to 30.8°C) and reduced dissolved oxygen (mean: 8.35 mg/L), indicative of eutrophic conditions. In contrast, winter and spring exhibited lower Chl-a levels associated with cooler temperatures and more stable oxygen conditions. The mean total phosphorus concentration (0.03 mg/L) suggests phosphorus limitation, consistent with international eutrophication thresholds. Four satellite-based algorithms – Two-Band Ratio, Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI), Three-Band Difference Algorithm (3BDA), and Maximum Chlorophyll Index (MCI) – were evaluated using S2 and L8 imagery. Sentinel-2 consistently outperformed Landsat-8, with NDCI achieving RMSE of 1.23 mg/m³, MAE of 0.93 mg/m³, and R² of 0.68. Seasonal validation identified fall as the most reliable period for Chl-a estimation (RMSE: 0.88–1.03 mg/m³), while winter showed the lowest errors but limited explanatory power (R²: 0.23–0.28). Landsat-8 yielded acceptable performance, particularly in spring (R²: 0.64–0.84), despite its coarser spatial resolution. Spatial Chl-a maps derived from NDCI revealed consistent distribution patterns between satellites and strong agreement with in-situ measurements. However, Sentinel-2’s finer spatial resolution (10–20 m) enabled improved detection of small-scale variability. Overall, the results highlight the value of Sentinel-2 red-edge bands for Chl-a retrieval in optically complex inland waters, while confirming the continued importance of Landsat-8 for long-term trend analysis. The findings emphasize the need for local calibration and support integrated satellite – in-situ monitoring frameworks for improved eutrophication management in urban lakes.

nodes.name: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

nodes.name: Blood biomarkers of long COVID: A cross-sectional evaluation of key cytokines and the coordination of inflammation
nodes.venue: PLOS One
nodes.abstract: Introduction Long COVID is a complex pathophysiological condition linked to a heterogenous symptom profile. Dysregulation of 1) immunological and inflammatory responses, 2) endothelial/vascular function, and 3) metabolic and clotting processes have been identified; however, there remains a lack of clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers. The study aim was to investigate dysregulation of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in confirmed Long COVID cases grouped by disease severity. Methods One-hundred-and-twenty-seven participants provided venous blood samples for cytokine profiling utilising Luminex assays. Participants were grouped into those with no knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 infection (n = 21), acute infection within 3-months (n = 22), spontaneous resolvers (>3-months, n = 21) and those with confirmed Long COVID (n = 63). Long COVID severity was grouped according to the post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) and defined as those with negligible (4A; n = 9), mild (4B; n = 20), moderate (4C; n = 24), and severe limitations (4D; n = 10). Cytokines were assessed for normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests and differences measured between groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests. Pairwise correlation and principal component analysis were performed. Results Interleukin-12 (p40/p70) was 22% greater in the Long COVID group (Median [IQR]: 58 [49] pg/mL, p = 0.046) and 30% greater in the acutely infected group (64 [36] pg/mL; p = 0.039) against non-infected controls (45 [25] pg/mL). Following PCFS classification, fibroblast growth factor-basic was 25% lower in Long COVID 4B versus spontaneous resolvers (24 [7] vs. 32 [24] pg/mL; p = 0.025). Pairwise correlation differences demonstrated that three Long COVID subgroups had strong, positive associations between cytokines when compared to non-infected controls; however, PCA was unable to determine any coordinated cytokine variation that was group specific. Discussion and conclusions Elevated interleukin-12 (p40/p70) and reduced basic fibroblast growth factor suggest persistent immune activation and possible subgroup-specific Long COVID; however, these findings were marginally significant and exploratory. A coordinated but partial immunological/inflammatory profile may exist in some of those with Long COVID, suggesting a rationale for subgrouping upon a biological, rather than self-report basis but larger longitudinal studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.

nodes.name: Apparent thermal thresholds of carbon sink weakening in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area revealed by remote sensing and spatial machine learning
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
nodes.abstract: Extreme summer heat poses a growing threat to terrestrial carbon sequestration, particularly in the forest and mountainous ecosystems of rapidly urbanizing subtropical regions, yet the spatial variability of heat-induced carbon-cycle responses and associated thermal threshold-like behavior remain insufficiently quantified. This study examined the effects of extreme summer heat on carbon cycling in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) during summer 2023 using multi-source remote sensing and ERA5 reanalysis data processed through Google Earth Engine. A total of 4,158 spatially representative samples covering urban cores, suburban transition zones, and peripheral forested ecological areas were analyzed using an integrated framework combining geographically weighted regression (GWR), GW-XGBoost nonlinear prediction, SHAP explainability, and Q 10 -based carbon budget accounting. Land surface temperature (LST) was identified as one of the key factors associated with reduced net primary productivity (NPP), showing a strong negative correlation with NPP ( r = −0.68, p < 0.001), whereas NDVI exhibited a strong positive association ( r = 0.72). The LST–NPP relationship was nonlinear, with a SHAP-identified transition interval near 27 °C –28 °C marking the onset of accelerated NPP decline, which progresses to substantially larger reductions at higher temperatures. Q10-based carbon budget estimates indicate that NPP falls below soil respiration—an indicator of source-like behavior—as surface temperature approaches 32 °C (estimated switch temperature, B switch = 32.05 °C). Across the sampled locations, 93.6% were estimated to be carbon sinks and 6.4% carbon sources, with the latter concentrated primarily in urban heat island areas along the Pearl River estuary. Strong sinks were concentrated in the northern mountainous forest belt, indicating that forest carbon-sink stability along urban–forest gradients is a key determinant of regional carbon balance. These findings highlight spatially uneven carbon vulnerability and support targeted heat mitigation, forest conservation, and adaptive-management strategies in subtropical megacity regions.

An Efficient Lightweight Framework for Cotton Weed Localization and Classification Using Multi-Scale Dual Attention Vision Transformer and Enhanced Haze Optimization
nodes.venue: Engineering Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Weed infestation significantly affects cotton productivity and increases crop management costs, highlighting the need for accurate and computationally efficient automated weed detection systems. This study proposes a lightweight unified framework for cotton weed localization and species classification by integrating EfficientNetB0, a Multi-Scale Dual Attention Vision Transformer (MS-DaViT), and an Enhanced Haze Optimization Algorithm (EHOA). The framework is designed to improve feature representation, weed localization, fine-grained species recognition, and hyperparameter selection under complex agricultural conditions. Experiments on the CottonWeedID15 dataset, comprising 5,187 images across 15 weed categories, demonstrate strong performance, achieving 98.9% mAP@50, 93.5% mAP@50–95, 98.75% classification accuracy, 98.53% precision, 98.62% recall, and 98.55% F1-score. Moreover, the framework contains only 0.80 million trainable parameters and achieves a measured GPU inference latency of 1.5 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 workstation under the reported experimental configuration. These results demonstrate computational efficiency on the evaluated GPU platform; validation on representative edge hardware is required before claiming edge-device deployment suitability.

nodes.name: A preliminary study on a synergistic assimilation scheme for multi-band satellite soil moisture data
nodes.venue: Geoscientific Model Development
nodes.abstract: Soil moisture retrievals from satellite sensors operating at different microwave frequencies provide diverse and complementary data sources for assimilation. However, fully exploiting the advantages of each frequency band while increasing the volume of assimilated observations remains a challenge. This study assimilates soil-moisture retrievals from three dominant-frequency instruments – SMAP (Soil Moisture Active–Passive), ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer), and MWRI (Microwave Radiation Imager) – into the Common Land Model (CoLM) via the Simplified Extended Kalman Filter (SEKF). Based on the systematic assessment of the disparate impacts of each single-band product, we propose and test a synergistic multi-satellite assimilation framework that optimally combines the complementary information inherent in the multi-frequency observations. Results show that assimilating soil-moisture retrievals improves the accuracy of the CoLM land-surface model; nevertheless, the effectiveness of each product varies with vegetation type. Analyses of simultaneous multi-source assimilation indicate that retrieval uncertainties associated with frequency-dependent differences in vegetation penetration capability are the dominant factor controlling the effectiveness of joint assimilation. When SMAP and ASCAT products are already ingested, the additional introduction of MWRI data over low-stature vegetation, where vegetation attenuation is relatively weak, provides complementary information and further enhances the joint assimilation performance. Validation against in-situ observations across China demonstrates that the largest improvements occur in the central and western parts of the country: compared with the open-loop simulation, the domain-mean correlation coefficient rises by about 0.25, while the error declines from 0.068 to 0.058 m 3 m −3 . This indicates that improvements from multi-sensor assimilation stem not only from increased data volume but also from the complementary characteristics of the assimilated products. These findings provide valuable insights into the design of synergistic multi-sensor land data assimilation systems and contribute to improving land surface modeling, as well as weather and climate prediction accuracy.

nodes.name: A Two Timescale Probabilistic State-Space Framework for Multimodal Affect Estimation and Uncertainty Aware Expressive Behavior in Humanoid Robots: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study
nodes.abstract: Abstract Humanoid robots intended for care, education and collaboration are expected to perceive human affect and respond appropriately, yet published systems often map momentary classifier outputs directly to robot expressions, discarding uncertainty, temporal structure and the asymmetric informativeness of sensing channels. This paper formulates affect transfer from human to robot as a Bayesian state-estimation and constrained-control problem. A six-dimensional latent state couples fast emotion and slow mood in pleasure–arousal–dominance (PAD) space; physiological, facial and vocal channels enter through modality-specific linear-Gaussian observation models; a sequential Kalman filter with a chi-square innovation gate fuses them under intermittent dropout and outliers; and an uncertainty-weighted, rate-limited mapping converts the posterior into robot display commands. The framework is evaluated entirely in synthetic Monte Carlo simulation (200 trials, 120 s each) under explicitly stated assumptions; no human-subject data are used. Under nominal conditions the gated fused filter reached an overall PAD RMSE of 0.151, against 0.257 for smoothed late fusion and 0.243 for a face-only filter. A 2 factorial study (R2 = 0.862) showed that gating helps only when outliers are present and slightly harms accuracy otherwise. Confidence scaling with λ = 2 cut display jitter by 81% and wrong-sign valence displays by 42% at a 32% tracking-error cost. The contribution is a reproducible, falsifiable baseline that must next be tested on recorded human data.

nodes.name: A 1-km weekly dataset of floating Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri blooms in China’s marginal seas derived from multi-sensor satellite observations
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Floating macroalgae blooms, primarily caused by Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri, frequently occur in the marginal seas around China, posing significant ecological and economic challenges. However, a long-term, high-frequency monitoring dataset capable of capturing bloom seasonality, interannual variability, and rapid transport dynamics across multiple sea regions remains limited. In this study, we derived 1-km weekly mean U. prolifera and S. horneri dataset covering 2018 to 2025, generated from 85,868 multi-sensor satellite images acquired from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), and Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI). By integrating complementary observations from multiple satellite sensors, the dataset substantially improves temporal continuity and observation availability relative to single-sensor products, enabling more complete characterization of rapidly evolving macroalgal blooms. A two-step deep learning-based approach was employed to detect and distinguish U. prolifera and S. horneri, achieving >90% accuracy for both bloom extraction and species classification across sensors. Independent validation using hyperspectral Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) Ocean Color Instrument (OCI) and Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) data further supports the reliability of species discrimination. The pair-wise cross-sensor biomass comparisons show strong consistency, with R² > 0.8 for both species. The dataset reveals distinct spatiotemporal patterns of the two macroalgal species. U. prolifera blooms in the Yellow Sea exhibit a relatively consistent seasonal cycle from May to August, with rapid aggregation and dissipation and the highest biomass recorded in 2021, whereas S. horneri shows a broader and more variable distribution across the East China Sea, with record-high biomass observed in 2024. Weekly observations further resolve rapid bloom aggregation, transport, and dissipation processes that are difficult to capture using monthly composites. Weekly products provide a balance between temporal resolution and observational completeness, preserving short-term bloom variability while supporting consistent interannual comparisons. Compared with weekly products, monthly composites underestimated seasonal peak biomass by 24–50% for S. horneri and 12–52% for U. prolifera during 2018–2025. In contrast, daily products were more sensitive to short-term biomass fluctuations, which could alter the identification of the year with the highest boom intensity, highlighting the importance of temporal aggregation for robust interannual comparisons. Comparisons with previous studies and reported bloom events demonstrate that the dataset reliably reproduces observed spatial distributions and seasonal characteristics. By providing a high-resolution, weekly, and species-resolved dataset of floating macroalgae, this study offers a consistent observational foundation for investigating species-specific bloom dynamics, assessing their responses to environmental variability, and enabling data-driven management and early warning of macroalgal blooms in China’s marginal seas.

nodes.name: BEVTraj: Map-Free Multimodal Trajectory Prediction with Sensor-Derived BEV Context and Sparse Goal Reasoning
nodes.venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering
nodes.abstract: Abstract Trajectory prediction is a key task in autonomous driving, where a model must forecast plausible future motions of surrounding agents from dynamic histories and scene context. Many recent methods use high-definition (HD) maps to provide explicit road topology and semantic constraints, but such maps are costly to maintain, geographically limited, and difficult to update in changing environments. This paper presents Bird’s-Eye View Trajectory Prediction (BEVTraj), a map-free trajectory prediction framework that directly uses BEV features constructed from raw multi-sensor data. Since sensor-derived BEV features are dense and only implicitly structured, BEVTraj employs deformable attention to selectively aggregate agent-relevant spatial context from sparse locations rather than processing the entire BEV grid uniformly. In addition, a Sparse Goal Candidate Proposal (SGCP) module combines overlapping mode-wise anchor clusters with attention-based goal prediction to generate compact, scene-adaptive goal hypotheses. These goals are decoded and iteratively refined into multimodal trajectories, while trajectory-aware mode scoring and temporal consistency modeling improve confidence estimation and suppress abrupt, physically implausible refinement updates. Experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 Sensor show that BEVTraj achieves competitive results under a map-free setting without using pre-built HD maps, while ablation studies and qualitative analyses illustrate the roles of BEV context aggregation and sparse goal reasoning. The source code is available at https://github.com/Kongminsang/bevtraj.
